en: Now, the Śābarī-kavaca; the meditation: Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, the illustrious Vīrabhadra.
Virūpākṣī, Laṃ, Nikuṃbhinī, Ṣoḍaśī, Upacāriṇī, Varūthinī, Māṃsacarviṇī. Ceṃ, ceṃ, ceṃ, to Cāmalarāyī!
Wealth, wealth! Tremble, tremble! Cause [them] to enter! O giver of worlds to those dwelling in the three worlds! Summon, summon the thousands of millions of gods!
Draw forth, draw forth the ninety million gandharvas!
Haṃsaḥ, haṃsaḥ; so'haṃ, so'haṃ; protect all, protect me, protect me from spirits, protect me from planetary influences, protect me from piśācas.
Protect from the Śākinīs! Protect from the Ḍākinīs! Protect, protect from invisible and visible misfortunes! O Mahāśakti, protect! O Kavacaśakti, protect!
Protect Ojaṃbāla! Guruvāla!
Oṃ, protect Prasaha Hanumān!
[Protect] the illustrious Nātha, the three Gurus, Gaṇapati, the three Pīṭhas, and Bhairava.
The mandala is enriched by the Siddhas, consisting of the pair of feet of the three Baṭukas and the triple radiance.
I bow to the circle of the Guru, accompanied by the four groups of eight Vairāṭas, the Nakta, the fivefold Vairāvalī, and the glorious Mālinī, the king of mantras;
thus is the meditation.
Now the prayer: Oṃ rhāṃ, rhīṃ, rhṛṃ, kṣāṃ, kṣīṃ, kṣuṃ. Salutation to Kṛṣṇakṣetrapāla; come, come!
O powerful one, pacifier of all planetary influences, perform my task, perform it! Svāhā!
Oṃ namo oṃ r̥hīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ Cakreśvarī!
You who hold the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus!
Grant me the fulfillment of my desires, grant it, svāhā!

Oṃ, salutations to the lotus-faced one, the enchantress who brings all people under her control, the manifest one of subtle form; by whom I am brought under her sway, Oṃ, may [all] become intoxicated with devotion, svāhā!
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the Lord Maheśvara;
the Guru is the manifest Supreme Brahman—salutations to that illustrious Guru.
Salutation to that illustrious Guru, by whom the eye of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance was opened with the probe of the ointment of knowledge.
The open space is suffused by a web of reddish morning rays;
she holds a rosary and a betel-roll, with a book in her hand;
her other hand is graced by a full-blown white lotus.
May the young girl, whose nature is eternally auspicious, dwell within my heart.
Now follows the application (viniyoga) for the recitation of the Śābarī-kavaca.
Śrī.
Now begins the recitation of the Śābarī-kavaca.
Oṃ! For the destruction of all obstacles; for the warding off of all misfortunes;
for the bestowing of all happiness; for the granting of intelligence to children;
and for the granting of various kinds of wealth, vehicles, and lands.
To the bestower of the fruits desired by the mind: protect, protect, svāhā! Oṃ, obeisance to the Guru. Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Oṃ, obeisance to Balabhadra. Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Rāma.
Oṃ, salutations to Hanumān. Oṃ, salutations to Śiva.
Oṃ, salutations to Jagannātha. Oṃ, salutations to Badrinārāyaṇa.
Oṃ, salutations to the goddess Durgā. Oṃ, salutations to Sūrya.
Oṃ, homage to Candra. Oṃ, homage to Bhauma.
Oṃ, homage to Budha. Oṃ, homage to Guru.
Oṃ, homage to Bhṛgu. Oṃ, homage to Śanaiścara.
Oṃ, homage to Rāhu! Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the Tail! Oṃ, perform protection for the nine planets, perform it, homage!
Oṃ, I consider even Hari, Hara, and the others to be superior when seen thus.
Upon seeing you, my heart finds satisfaction; what is the use of looking further at others on this earth? O Lord, no one else captivates the mind; therefore, come to me.
Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Balabhadra, Jaya, Vijaya, and Aparājita!
May there be well-being; grant us well-being, grant us well-being, svāhā!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ.
May he impel our thoughts.
Pacify all obstacles, pacify them, svāhā!
Oṃ aiṃ, r̥hīṃ, klīṃ, śrī, to Baṭukabhairava, for the removal of calamities, to the Great Sky-like One, to the Essential Form.
Destroy, destroy long-lasting misfortune! O bestower of various kinds of enjoyments! Strike down, strike down all my misfortunes! Cook, cook! Seize, seize! Bind, bind! Kaca kaca!
At the king’s gate, bring victory, bring victory! In legal proceedings, increase profit, increase profit!
In battle, destroy the enemy, destroy the enemy!
Avert, avert the connection with non-offenses! Produce, produce the arising of the mental continuum! Fulfill, fulfill the lifespan! Grant, grant the attainment of a woman! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vāsudeva; homage! Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Nārāyaṇa, whose form is the universe!
To Śrī Puruṣottama, protect, protect!
Whatever is under your control, whether perceptible or imperceptible:
digest, digest!
O you whose form is the universe, slay, slay the enemies!
Destroy, destroy the fever that occurs every day, every two days, every three days, and every four days!
Strike down, strike down the four additional types of wind-disorders, the eighteen wasting diseases, and the eighteen types of leprosy! Shatter, shatter all the humors! Destroy, destroy all of that!
Dry it up, dry it up! Draw it forth, draw it forth!
Kill my enemy, kill him! Drive him away, drive him away! Cause hatred, cause hatred! Paralyze, paralyze! Ward off, ward off!
Slay, slay the obstacles! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Grind, grind! Destroy, destroy! Put to flight, put to flight!
Seizing the discus, come quickly, come quickly! Slay, slay with the discus!
Cut, cut the false sciences!
Shatter, destroy the eighty-four classes of servants!
[Destroy] those whose vision is struck by wind-pains!
Of serpents, lions, tigers, bipeds, and quadrupeds; others, whether external or internal, moving on earth or in the atmosphere;
and yet others situated in various places and times.
Slay, slay all! [Slay] the uneven clouds, rivers, mountains, and so forth;
the eight diseases; all locations; and the thieves on the paths by night and day—bring them under control, bring them under control!
Destroy, destroy all calamities! Tear asunder, tear asunder the enemy army! Ward off, ward off the hostile forces! Burn, burn; provide protection, provide protection!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One; Oṃ, homage to Nārāyaṇa, huṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ! Oṃ rhāṃ rhīṃ, [homage] to one’s own deity in the heart.

This Vidyā called Mahānāmī was given of old to Śatakratu; having slain all those Bala-Dānavas, it slays the Asuras. That man who, self-restrained, constantly recites this Vaiṣṇavī [Vidyā], [attains his goal].
Indeed, she destroys all whose sight is poisoned by her gaze;
furthermore, one who possesses the poison of another’s gaze must certainly not be allowed to cross over her.
When worn upon the body in battle, she herself pacifies portents of misfortune.
Supreme good fortune arises for him; of this there is no doubt.
When he invokes [the deity], victory is immediate for him, and no obstacle shall arise for him.
What is the use of much speaking here? All forms of auspicious prosperity belong to him.
One obtains this, there is no doubt in this; it shall not be otherwise when [the drum] resounds.
Even if effort is exerted by children in various ways,
that which is cold becomes hot, and that which is hot becomes cold.
The knowledge (vidyā) that I have declared is not heard elsewhere by one who would recite it.
One should write this yantra with gorocana on birch bark;
by binding this vidyā upon the head, may it grant me protection from all [harm].
Whether bound on the hand of a man or a woman, the wise one [is protected]:
they flee and perish, while Dharma remains forever;
all fear of enemies departs, and they quickly take to flight.
Oṃ Aiṃ, Rhīṃ, Klīṃ, Śrīṃ, to Bhuvaneśvarī! Śrīṃ Oṃ, salutations again and again to Bhairava! Now follows the Śrīmātaṅgī-bheda, the twenty-two-syllable mantra.
Or [it may be] from the *svāhākṛti* at the conclusion of the sacrifice.
Hari Oṃ. Salutation to Ucciṣṭadevī.
To Ḍākinī, Sumukhidevī, and Mahāpiśācinī.
Oṃ Aiṃ, Rhīṃ, Ṭhāḥ, Ṭhaḥ—twenty-two [syllables] for Oṃ Cakrīdharā.
I perform protection, perform protection!
Homage, homage to the Goddess who removes all afflictions!
Perform the pacification of all kinds of obstacles and the warding off of misfortune, perform, perform!
Phaṭ! Śrī Oṃ, to the goddess Kubjikā, rhīṃ ṭhaḥ svaḥ! Swiftly ward off misfortune, kuru kuru!
To the goddess Śābarī, kīṃ ṭhaḥ svaḥ!
O Māyā, destroy this physical sense of duality; grant me a full lifespan!
Perform the root-protection of Hemavatī!
Homage to the goddess Cāmuṇḍā!
Swiftly ward off obstacles! Protect against all wind, phlegm, and bile disorders! Strike down the bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas! Quell the effects of sorcery and curses!
O Satī, for Sarasvatī and the goddess Caṇḍikā, [remove] the throat-pustules; having observed them, bring about their pacification! Bring about the destruction of the great fever, svāhā!
All-encompassing abundance, truth! Day by day, give, give! Protect, protect!
Moment by moment, ward off misfortune!
Day by day, perform the removal of suffering, the bringing of auspiciousness, and the accomplishment of all tasks!
Hari Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Rāmacandra!
Hari Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ!
To the Goddess Śeṣanāga-Pṛthvī, who dwells in the sky along with the moon, stars, and the nine planets— pacify all misfortunes, Svāhā!
Longevity, health, sovereignty, wealth, knowledge, fame, and strength.
Standing in water reaching up to the navel, one should perform it a thousand times.
One should recite this armor-mantra daily; from that, perfection of speech shall arise.
By this method, through devotion, the accomplishment of the mantra is also attained.
Whoever recites it one hundred times is liberated; there is no doubt about this.
In every place of fear caused by all diseases, one should indeed contemplate this with the mind.
Kings come under one's control for the sake of accomplishing all desires and goals.
By this recitation performed according to my ability, may the goddess Śābarī be pleased; salutations to her.
May it be auspicious! Thus ends the Śābarī-kavaca.
